title: Ash-Shakur, the Appreciative
hookLine: the Appreciative, rewarding the smallest good
tomorrow: why say 'Most High' with your forehead on the floor?

lines: THE BIN BACK FROM THE CURB.
cards: The barista who remembers your order. The neighbor who drags your bin back from the curb. Small things, and the thank-you that would fit them usually never gets said.
Yesterday's question: a man, a thirsty dog, a shoe full of water, who says thank you? Here's the hadith. A man on the road, dying of thirst, finds a well, climbs down, and drinks.
Back up top, a dog is panting, licking the damp ground. The man thinks: this dog is as thirsty as I was.
So he climbs down again, fills his leather shoe with water, holds it in his teeth, climbs back up, and lets the dog drink.

teach.b: And the hadith says, plainly: Allah thanked him, and forgave him. That's the line to tell a friend tonight. In this story, God is the one who says thank you.
That's today's Name. Ash-Shakur, the Appreciative, who rewards the smallest good. Not a big donation, not a well-known deed.
One shoe of water for one dog, and it's noticed. The companions were surprised too. Is there reward for us even with animals? they asked.
In every living being, the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, said, there is reward.

And in another hadith he said: don't look down on any good deed, even meeting your brother with a cheerful face. So the smallest good has a witness who appreciates it. And thanks runs the other way too.
The Prophet said that whoever doesn't thank people hasn't thanked Allah. Shukr, gratitude, isn't a feeling saved for prayer. It's a note on a locker, a word to the person who stayed late.
If Ash-Shakur notices a shoe of water, nothing anyone does for you is too small to notice back.

how: Muslims practice shukr, thanking Allah with words like alhamdulillah and by thanking people; the story of the man who watered a thirsty dog is retold to teach that no good deed is too small.

o: the Appreciative, rewarding the smallest good
the one who rewards only large good deeds
the one who is thankful only to His prophets

games.q: who did what at the well — tap the pairs.

s: in Islam, kindness to an animal earns nothing
in every living being there is reward, the Prophet said.
the hadith says Allah thanked the man who watered the dog
Allah thanked him, and forgave him.
gratitude is owed to Allah alone, so thanking people doesn't matter
whoever doesn't thank people hasn't thanked Allah.

games.q: a kid in your class drops a couple of coins in the fundraiser jar, and someone laughs at how little it is. what fits Ash-Shakur?
o: it doesn't really count; only big gifts make a difference.
say nothing; whether it counts is between him and God.
it counts; the Appreciative rewards the smallest good.
games.why: one shoe of water for one dog was thanked. don't look down on any good deed, the Prophet said.

practice: Pour a glass of water, or pick up whatever you're drinking. Take a slow sip and notice it all: how cool it is, its weight on your tongue, the swallow.
With each sip through the sit, let one person who made your day a little easier come to mind, and thank them silently by name.

wordCard.voice: Ash-Shakur. The Appreciative, who thanked a man for a shoe of water and rewards the smallest good.

orig.note: Arabic: the Appreciative, the one who thanks and rewards even the smallest good.

carryVoice: Hold on to this: nothing is too small, not the good you do and not the good done for you. Day fifteen-oh-nine is in.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 2363; Sahih Muslim 2244 (the man who watered a thirsty dog: Allah thanked him and forgave him; in every living being there is reward)
Sahih Muslim 2626 (do not belittle any good deed, even meeting your brother with a cheerful face)
Sunan Abi Dawud 4811 (whoever does not thank people has not thanked Allah)
Jami' at-Tirmidhi 3507 (ash-Shakur in the list of the Names)
